clue.text: Small and not initially serious revolutionary, part of Churchill and Kipling's lives

definitions.text: part of Churchill and Kipling's lives

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns right round, so the whole assembly is read backwards

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: not initially says the opening letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: a serious situation can be called tragic

explanation.surface: A small, half-hearted radical gets a walk-on part in the lives of two great Britons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not initially' strips T from TRAGIC to leave RAGIC; S plus RAGIC is SRAGIC, and 'revolutionary' turns it all round.
explanation.definitionFit: Churchill was rarely seen without a cigar, and Kipling wrote that a good cigar is a smoke, so the habit featured in both men's lives.

clue.text: A portion of rich orangeade that's vital for Olympians

indicators.note: A portion of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A glass of rich orange drink is said to keep the gods going.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the gods of Olympus had an ethereal fluid in their veins instead of blood, the stuff that kept them alive.

clue.text: Albert hit heavyweight critic of Lawrence, twice

parts.note: Al is the usual short form of the name Albert
to ding is to strike or dent something
a ton is a very heavy weight

explanation.surface: A boxer called Albert lands a punch on a big man who has been attacking Lawrence.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Aldington wrote hostile books on both D. H. Lawrence and T. E. Lawrence, hence 'twice'.
explanation.definitionFit: The writer Richard Aldington produced critical biographies of two famous men named Lawrence, the novelist and Lawrence of Arabia.

clue.text: "An epergne or centre-piece (…) so heavily overhung with cobwebs that its form was quite undistinguishable; (…) I saw — legged spiders with blotchy bodies running home to it" (Great Expectations)

definitions.text: "An epergne or centre-piece (…) so heavily overhung with cobwebs that its form was quite undistinguishable; (…) I saw — legged spiders with blotchy bodies running home to it" (Great Expectations)

parts.words: "An epergne or centre-piece (…) so heavily overhung with cobwebs that its form was quite undistinguishable; (…) I saw — legged spiders with blotchy bodies running home to it" (Great Expectations)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Pip's description of Miss Havisham's decaying wedding table: the missing word describes the spiders' spotted legs

explanation.surface: A passage from Dickens describing the cobwebbed wedding cake in Miss Havisham's room, with one word missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens calls the spiders marked with small spots on their legs by a word meaning dotted or flecked.

clue.text: East Coker — extremely drawn out, a poem about death

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for East on a compass

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged
extremely means take the letters at the extremes of the word

explanation.surface: Eliot's East Coker is described as a long-drawn-out meditation on mortality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes D and N from 'drawn'; 'out' scrambles them with COKER to give DENROCK. Eden Rock is Charles Causley's poem about his dead parents.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Causley's late poem imagines his dead mother and father waiting for him across a stream, a quiet meditation on dying.

clue.text: Irish Republican's son pursues relatives embraced by Irish youngsters

indicators.note: pursues means the son comes after everything else
embraced by means the relatives sit inside the word for Irish

parts.note: Erse is an old name for the Irish Gaelic language
kin are one's family members
childer is a dialect plural of child, common in Ireland
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: An Irish rebel's boy tags along behind cousins who are being hugged by Irish children.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'. Robert Erskine Childers, author of The Riddle of the Sands, was executed in 1922 as a Republican.
explanation.definitionFit: The novelist was shot by the Free State government for his role on the anti-Treaty side during the Irish Civil War.

clue.text: A slip on a slip?

parts.note: a mistake (a slip) noted on a separate slip of paper inserted into a printed book

explanation.surface: Someone loses their footing twice in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: A printer's correction notice lists a mistake and is often a loose sheet tipped into the volume.

clue.text: I'm prepared to be the saviour of a ship-wrecked family

definitions.meaning: a way of declaring oneself set to go

definitions.text: the saviour of a ship-wrecked family
definitions.meaning: Masterman ..., the old seaman who saves the Seagrave family in Captain Marryat's novel

explanation.definitionFit: Being prepared is the plain sense; Marryat named the castaways' rescuer Masterman Ready in his children's novel.

clue.text: St Augustine's work in Canterbury?

definitions.meaning: the famous treatise by Augustine of Hippo, De Civitate Dei
Canterbury, seat of the Church of England's senior archbishop, could fairly be called a holy city

explanation.definitionFit: Augustine of Hippo's great Latin treatise translates as this title, and a cathedral city like Canterbury fits it playfully.

clue.text: Play in which we see Her Ladyship artfully herd steers

definitions.text: Play in which we see Her Ladyship

indicators.note: artfully means arranged with skill, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drama in which an aristocratic lady cleverly drives cattle.
explanation.walkthrough: Ronald Harwood's play is set backstage with an ageing actor-manager; his wife is known as Her Ladyship.
explanation.definitionFit: Ronald Harwood's backstage drama features the leading actor's wife, addressed throughout by her title.

clue.text: Boho's quietly leaving a social event

indicators.note: leaving means the letter for quietly goes out of the word

parts.note: a party is a social gathering
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly

explanation.surface: A bohemian slips away discreetly from a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Boho is short for bohemian, describing a pretentiously artistic style.

clue.text: Corrupt king retains territory in Africa

indicators.note: Corrupt means spoilt or altered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A crooked monarch hangs on to land in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retains' looks like a container signal but is fodder: K plus RETAINS rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a nominally independent black homeland in South Africa under apartheid.

clue.text: A water poet's articulated cutter

indicators.note: articulated means spoken, so the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a cutter is one who cuts cloth for clothes, a garment maker

explanation.surface: A poet who writes about water has a well-spoken pair of scissors.
explanation.walkthrough: John Taylor (1578-1653) was a Thames waterman who wrote verse and called himself the Water Poet. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: John Taylor, a London boatman turned versifier, was known in his day as the Water Poet.

clue.text: Malcolm Bradbury's novel with a drunk French dedicatee?

definitions.meaning: Bradbury's last novel, about Diderot's journey to Catherine the Great's St Petersburg
a toast drunk to Hermitage, the French red wine from the Rhone

explanation.definitionFit: Bradbury's final novel has this title, and raising a glass to a Rhone wine would be worded the same way.

clue.text: In a Shaw play, she gives advice to a lecher running wild

definitions.text: In a Shaw play, she gives advice

indicators.note: running wild means out of control, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman in a Shaw drama counsels a lecherous man who has run amok.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oracle is a character in Shaw's Back to Methuselah.
explanation.definitionFit: In Back to Methuselah Shaw has a prophetess figure consulted for guidance.

clue.text: Ohio and Tennessee in an Emerson poem

definitions.meaning: Ralph Waldo Emerson's poem contrasting the Musketaquit with a spiritual stream

explanation.definitionFit: The Ohio and Tennessee are a pair of American watercourses, and Emerson's poem has that title.

clue.text: Who went round with TV dinner for a poor scholar?

indicators.note: went round suggests turning about, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Someone circulated a microwave meal to feed an impoverished academic.
explanation.walkthrough: Vernon Whitford is the penniless scholar cousin in George Meredith's The Egoist.
explanation.definitionFit: In Meredith's The Egoist this character is Sir Willoughby's impecunious, bookish cousin.

clue.text: An old description of West part of Islington, negative at first

indicators.note: at first means the negative word is placed at the front

parts.note: no is a negative reply
the Angel is a district of Islington in north London, named after an old coaching inn

explanation.surface: An old account of the western side of Islington, which begins by saying no.
explanation.walkthrough: West is Mae West, star of the 1933 film I'm No Angel, hence 'old'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mae West's 1933 film title describes her as anything but saintly.

clue.text: Ain't it a strange lady who appears in a play about Robin Hood

definitions.text: lady who appears in a play about Robin Hood

indicators.note: strange means odd or altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Isn't it odd that a woman turns up in a drama about the outlaw of Sherwood?
explanation.walkthrough: The Robin is not the outlaw but Robin Goodfellow, Puck, in A Midsummer Night's Dream, where the fairy queen appears.
explanation.definitionFit: The queen of the fairies in A Midsummer Night's Dream, which also features the sprite Robin Goodfellow.

clue.text: Supporter protecting a monarch in an Emerson poem

indicators.note: protecting means wrapping round, so the second part goes inside the first

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
HM is the abbreviation for His or Her Majesty

explanation.surface: A bodyguard shields a king who features in Emerson's verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Emerson wrote a short poem named after the Hindu creator god.

clue.text: A language which India uses

indicators.note: uses says the letters are held within the words before it

explanation.surface: A tongue spoken in the subcontinent.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the official tongues of the Indian republic.

clue.text: Doesn't dispute permit to meet and work

parts.note: to let is to allow
a committee sits when it meets
a machine that goes is working

explanation.surface: A licence to convene and get on with business is not challenged.
explanation.definitionFit: To let something go is an idiom for not pursuing or arguing about it.

clue.text: Have a lot of food such as Cheddar

definitions.meaning: Cheddar ... is a limestone ravine in Somerset, England

explanation.definitionFit: To eat greedily is to stuff oneself, and Cheddar in Somerset gives its name to a famous ravine.

clue.text: Finally, poetess may follow appropriate rules

indicators.note: Finally points to the closing letter of the word next to it

parts.note: can and may both express being permitted

explanation.surface: In the end a woman poet may obey the conventions.
explanation.definitionFit: Verse that scans keeps to the proper metrical pattern.

clue.text: The Rev W. Awdry's classic bildungsroman?

definitions.text: The Rev W. Awdry's classic bildungsroman?

parts.words: The Rev W. Awdry's classic bildungsroman?
parts.note: Gottfried Keller's coming-of-age novel shares its title with a description of one of the engines in Awdry's railway stories, the green one

explanation.surface: A children's author is credited with a weighty German coming-of-age novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Keller's Der grüne Heinrich is a classic Swiss bildungsroman; Henry in Awdry's Thomas the Tank Engine books is green.
explanation.definitionFit: Keller's novel title in English matches the colour and name of an engine from Awdry's railway series.

clue.text: Marina is the most important feature of a Greek port for this hero

definitions.text: Marina is the most important feature of a Greek port for this hero

parts.words: Marina is the most important feature of a Greek port for this hero
parts.note: Marina is the long-lost daughter of Shakespeare's Prince of Tyre, his greatest treasure; the surface reads her as a harbour for yachts

explanation.surface: A yacht harbour is the main attraction of a Greek seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Marina looks like a boat harbour, but she is the daughter whom Shakespeare's hero, Prince of Tyre, finds again.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's late play is named after the prince whose daughter Marina is restored to him.

clue.text: In literature, the lady with the golden gun?

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
the Sten is a British submachine gun

explanation.surface: A literary heroine is armed with a gold-plated pistol.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the Bond title The Man with the Golden Gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Austen is the pre-eminent woman of English letters, often called simply the lady novelist.
